text.p: Scientific-Atlanta Inc Thursday reported a 165 percent increase in first quarter earnings from continuing operations on an 8 percent increase in sales to $261.7 million.
"We are very pleased with our performance during the quarter. We had strong bookings, improved margins, and a healthy book-to-bill ratio," chief executive James F. McDonald said.
Bookings for the quarter were $285.0 million, up 41 percent over 1996's first quarter, the company said.

"Gross margins of 30.1 percent improved 5 percentage points over last year's first quarter, reflecting the impact of internal programs to improve our quality and cost structure as well as the ramp-up of our Juarez manufacturing facility, McDonald said.

"Partially offsetting the margin improvement was our continued investment in R&D programs, up 23 percent from last year and 14 percent sequentially, to support our ambitious new product initiatives. We expect to continue significant R&D investments and anticipate start-up costs as these new products are rolled out."
